subject: Clarifying Redwood default retention for requests vs outputs
messages:
From: Sara Connors <sara.connors@brightbank.com>

Cc: security@brightbank.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: what does Redwood keep by default (requests vs outputs)?

Hi Jonas,

We're finishing our internal security review and a few reviewers flagged a question on Redwood's default retention for hosted API traffic. Specifically they want a concise answer to: which elements are stored by default and for how long (user requests, model prompts, streaming tokens, final outputs, embeddings, attachments)? Also: are any of those replicated outside the customer's region by default?

We need something short we can attach to the questionnaire (one-paragraph + bullets). Can you confirm?

Thanks — Sara
Sara Connors
Senior InfoSec Program Manager, BrightBank

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Sara Connors <sara.connors@brightbank.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Quick Q: what does Redwood keep by default (requests vs outputs)?

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask. Below is an answer you can paste into your questionnaire. I also copied Kim and Karthik for regional/operational notes. If you want this shorter, tell me and I will trim.

One-paragraph summary (paste-able):
Redwood's hosted default capture window is limited and purpose-built for operational troubleshooting and quality monitoring: by default, authenticated hosted API requests and the corresponding final model outputs are retained for 60 days. Streaming tokens (intermediate partial tokens) are not persisted beyond the live session unless a customer explicitly enables debug capture. Derived artifacts such as embeddings or indexes are not created or stored by default unless the customer opts into "persist outputs" features; attachments referenced in requests are retained only if uploaded to our storage and follow the same 60-day window. We store logs within the request's configured region by default and do not copy hosted request/response content to other regions except for rare failover cases governed by documented cross-region routing policies.

Bulleted breakdown:
- User requests (raw prompts): retained by default for 60 days (hosted) for troubleshooting and billing reconciliation.
- Final model outputs (responses): retained by default for 60 days.
- Streaming/intermediate tokens: ephemeral — not persisted after the session unless debug capture is enabled.
- Embeddings/index artifacts: not stored by default; only if customer explicitly requests persistent indexing.
- Attachments uploaded to Redwood: retained under the same 60-day window unless a customer requests earlier deletion.
- Cross-region replication: not performed for request/response content under normal operation; exceptions are documented in our routing SLA and require customer opt-in for multi-region failover.

If you'd like, I can attach the short retention matrix and a SOC2-friendly checklist for evidence redaction.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Customer Success (Security Liaison), Redwood Inference

Sara,

Thanks for the patience — attaching a short retention matrix and a SOC2-friendly redaction checklist (see attachments). Final clarifications based on Kim's notes:
- Region residency: for customers who select an EU or APAC hosted region, request/response content and associated artifacts are stored in that region by default and are not copied to other regions for analytics. Cross-region replication only happens when a customer enables multi-region failover or when capacity-based failover is triggered and the customer has agreed to the documented routing policy.
- Debug capture: explicit opt-in. Debug captures are tagged with restricted ACLs and a shorter retention window (30 days) for security review artifacts.
- Deletion requests: customers can request earlier erasure via the Console (Data & Privacy tab) or by opening a ticket — we execute erasure workflows and provide a confirmation export.

Attachment stubs:
- retention-matrix-brief.xlsx (attachment: retention matrix by artifact type and region)
- SOC2-redaction-checklist.pdf (attachment: checklist to help BrightBank prepare evidence for auditors)

If you want a one-line summary to paste into the questionnaire: 
"By default Redwood retains hosted API requests and final outputs for 60 days within the customer's chosen region; streaming tokens are ephemeral and debug capture requires explicit opt-in with restricted access and a 30-day debug retention window."

Happy to jump on a 20-min call if your team prefers.

Best,
